evals.prompt: Review only violations of the accepted observability contract. Contract: route metrics use route templates plus bounded outcome/error labels; logs are structured and exclude credentials, bodies, and raw tenant/user identifiers; W3C trace context and allowlisted baggage cross synchronous boundaries while async retries/redrives preserve lineage; invoice processing distinguishes attempts, durable handoff, final logical completion, DLQ depth/oldest age, and reconciliation; the completion SLI pages only after its event floor and links an owned dashboard/runbook; pprof is internal-only; shutdown performs a bounded exporter flush. Changed behavior uses r.URL.Path, X-Tenant-ID, and err.Error() as metric labels; logs Authorization and the raw body; replaces the outbound context with context.Background without propagation; increments the final-completion failure SLI on every retry; registers pprof on the public default mux; and shuts down the server without exporter flush. The new page fires on any failure sample and has no event floor, owner, dashboard, or runbook; DLQ and reconciliation expose retry counts only.
evals.expected_output: Report the bounded-label/privacy, trace-correlation, attempt-versus-logical-outcome and async visibility, alert actionability, debug exposure, and exporter-flush violations as observability findings.
assertions: Finds raw path, tenant ID, and error text as unsafe or unbounded metric labels and credential/body logging as a privacy violation
Finds lost caller trace propagation or correlation across the outbound boundary
Finds retry attempts misclassified as final logical failures and missing DLQ age/redrive/reconciliation outcome visibility
Finds the alert's missing event floor, owner, dashboard, or runbook against the accepted policy
Finds public debug exposure and missing bounded exporter flush proof
Keeps corrections on observability conformance and does not redesign reliability, security, or delivery policy

evals.prompt: Review only accepted observability behavior. Each changed path names an operator decision and uses stable structured logs, bounded metrics, safe trace/context propagation, coherent resource identity, and privacy-approved correlation. Attempt, durable handoff, retry, final logical outcome, freshness, DLQ/redrive, and reconciliation are distinct. SLIs measure the accepted promise; alerts have event floors, owners, dashboards, runbooks, and actions. Diagnostics are internal and access-controlled. Sampling, retention, label growth, and cost are bounded. Shutdown records drain and a bounded successful exporter flush. No telemetry policy is missing or changed.
evals.expected_output: Return no observability findings without padding, invented signal policy, or neighboring-domain warnings.
assertions: Does not invent signals, labels, SLO thresholds, alert policy, sampling, retention, or cost limits
Does not pad the result with security, reliability, performance, or delivery findings

evals.prompt: The accepted observability contract remains fully satisfied: attempts and final outcomes are distinct, all bounded signals and alert/runbook pivots remain intact, correlation is safe, and shutdown flushes telemetry. The changed request path replaces the inbound context with context.Background, retries every failure forever without a deadline, and ignores the accepted three-attempt end-to-end budget. Review owner arbitration only.
evals.expected_output: Name go-reliability-review as the single primary owner for the accepted deadline, cancellation, and retry-policy violations; emit no duplicate observability finding.
assertions: Names exactly go-reliability-review as the primary review owner
Identifies the decisive axis as accepted end-to-end context, deadline, cancellation, and retry behavior
Emits no duplicate observability finding because telemetry conformance is stated as preserved

evals.prompt: A new asynchronous settlement flow emits technically valid structured logs, metrics, and spans, but no accepted observability contract defines the operator decisions, logical success boundary, SLI good/total events, alert response, allowed labels or forensic identifiers, sampling/retention budget, DLQ/redrive signals, or shutdown flush obligation. No concrete leak or unbounded mechanism is shown. Review without choosing policy.
evals.expected_output: Hand off the missing signal, outcome, SLI/alert, privacy/cardinality, async, and flush policy to go-observability-spec without inventing it or filing a conformance defect.
assertions: Names go-observability-spec as the unresolved decision owner
Does not invent operator questions, success semantics, labels, SLOs, alerts, sampling, retention, async signals, or flush budgets
Does not report an observability conformance finding against policy that has not been accepted
